Section 4 • \(\xi\)3D

4.6 From per-sample to ensemble estimates

Suppose we have \(N\) realizations \(\{\delta_i^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda)\}_{s=1}^{N}\) of the fields on the same set of sightlines covering \(\mathcal{A}_\perp\). A natural estimator of the ensemble 3D 2PCF at transverse separation \(\vec{r}_{\perp}\) and spectral separation \(\Delta\) is then the average of the per-sample estimators: \begin{equation} \widehat{\xi}_{ij}\!\left(\vec{r}_{\perp},\Delta\right) \;\equiv\; \frac{1}{N}\sum_{s=1}^{N} \widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{r}_{\perp},\Delta\right), \tag{4.14} \end{equation} where \(\widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}(\vec{r}_{\perp},\Delta)\) is given by Eq. (4.2). Under the homogeneity of Eq. (4.13), every term in the window average of Eq. (4.2) has expectation \(\xi_{ij}(\vec{r}_{\perp},\Delta)\), so each per-sample estimator, and hence their average, is unbiased: \(\langle\widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}(\vec{r}_{\perp},\Delta)\rangle_{\rm ens}=\xi_{ij}(\vec{r}_{\perp},\Delta)\) (provided the \(\delta_i\) are built with the true mean fields; normalizing with means measured on the same sample introduces an integral-constraint bias at large separations). For independent realizations the variance of Eq. (4.14) decreases as \(1/N\), and the estimator converges to \(\xi_{ij}\) as \(N\to\infty\). In practice one usually has a single realization (\(N=1\)) and relies on ergodicity instead: the per-sample estimator approaches \(\xi_{ij}\) when the domain is large compared with the correlation length, i.e. when \(\mathcal{A}_\perp\) and \(L_\Lambda-|\Delta|\) contain many statistically independent patches, so that many effectively independent pairs contribute at the given lag. The identification therefore degrades for lags approaching the size of the domain (\(|\Delta|\to L_\Lambda\), or \(\vec{r}_{\perp}\) comparable to the extent of \(\mathcal{A}_\perp\)), where few pairs remain. Finally, if the statistics evolve with redshift, the estimator measures a pair-weighted average of \(\xi_{ij}(\vec{r}_{\perp},\Delta;\bar{\Lambda})\) over the interval, i.e. the correlation at an effective redshift.
